subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBank)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@finbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBank)

Hi Aisha / Devon —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can move to a short technical spike: 

Key pain points you described
- Token/unit economics: current provider costs are high — team estimates ~3–4x per-token spend compared to budget for production usage.
- Latency variability at peak (customer-facing features) causing timeouts and retries.
- Ops overhead around model variants and capacity planning — spikes during payroll cycles.

Current stack
- Front-end inference client -> internal API -> Hosted LLM provider (managed endpoints)
- Model: mix of open Llama-derived variant for chat + a smaller reranker per request
- No dedicated GPU pool; autoscaling with warmup latency (~6–8s) during bursts

Success criteria you mentioned
- 50%+ reduction in per-API-call inference cost (unit economics) or equivalent ROI via batching/caching
- Median p95 latency under 300ms for 256-token prompts during normal load; graceful degradation at peak
- Clear deployment path (hosted vs dedicated) that meets data isolation & audit needs

Technical preferences / openness
- Very open to batching and prefix/KV caching, provided user-facing latency for single-turn queries remains acceptable.
- Open to quantization if quality delta is within acceptable bounds for our risk profile — willing to run evals.
- Interested in Redwood’s autoscaling and routing policies to handle payroll-driven spikes.

Proposed next steps (we discussed):
1) Run a 2-week spike focused on unit economics and latency: Redwood will provide a small dedicated evaluation config (dedicated pool + batching/caching profile).
2) Ben (cc’d) will lead the technical setup and bench with your API traffic sample; need a representative 24-hour QPS trace.
3) We’ll run A/B with a subset of traffic (5–10%) and measure cost/perf deltas; share metrics dashboard links.
4) Quick follow-up call to review results and scope enterprise terms if positive.

Attachments: redwood_overview.pdf (high level), unit_economics_spike_plan.xlsx (spike milestones & metrics).

Could you confirm: 1) a contact for provisioning the traffic sample (SRE or eng lead)? 2) preferred dates to start the spike (we’re available 6/15–6/22 window)?

Thanks — looking forward to collaborating.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
